title: N.J.A.C. 5:23-3 Subcodes (incl. 5:23-3.16 Electrical subcode with NJ amendments to NEC 2023), current through 58 N.J.R. No.16 (Aug 17, 2026)
publisher: NJ Department of Community Affairs, Division of Codes and Standards
keyFacts: 5:23-3.16(a)1 adopts NFPA 'National Electrical Code (NEC) 2023' plus TIAs 70-23-1 through 70-23-13 as the NJ electrical subcode (p.208).
5:23-3.16(a)3 adopts the National Electrical Safety Code ANSI C2-2023 for utility area lighting on private property on metal poles with underground feed (p.208).
Informational Note references are explanatory only, not adopted (5:23-3.16(a)2i; text still says 'NEC 2020' - likely a drafting carryover) (p.208).
AHJ = the Electrical Subcode Official; 'qualified person' expanded to include one permitted to work under the NJ licensing law N.J.S.A. 45:5A (p.209).
Deleted NEC sections: 110.17 servicing/maintenance, 110.29 in-sight-from definition section (pp.209-210).
Deleted 210.12(E) (AFCI for branch-circuit extensions/modifications/replacements) and 406.4(D)(4) (AFCI on receptacle replacement) - NJ does not require AFCI upgrades for these (p.210).
Deleted 225.41 (emergency disconnects for outside branch circuits/feeders) (p.210).
300.4(A)(1) amended: bored holes in wood members as required by the building subcode; protection applies where the hole edge is less than 1-1/4 in. from the member edge (p.210).
Article 425 industrial process heating largely deleted; 514.3(B)(3) fuel storage (except (e)) deleted; 525.5(B) replaced with NEC 2005 15-ft clearance text (pp.210-211).
550 Part II (mobile homes) deleted except for repair/renovation/alteration; 551 RV parts II-V deleted; 552 applies to seasonal park trailers (p.212).
Deleted 680.4 (pool inspections after installation), 706.7 (ESS commissioning/maintenance), 805.156 (dwelling-unit communications outlet), and Informative Annex H (pp.212-213).
History: amended by R.2026 d.086, effective August 17, 2026 (58 N.J.R. 1898(a)); prior rewrite R.2022 d.111 effective Sept 6, 2022 (pp.216-217).
notes: Full subchapter 3 (all subcodes). Electrical subcode at PDF pp.208-217. NEC model text itself is NOT included (NFPA copyright). The TIA document on DCA's site (nec_2023_tia_1_13.pdf) is NFPA material and was not downloaded.

title: N.J.A.C. 5:23 Uniform Construction Code regulations (full chapter), current through 58 N.J.R. No.16 (Aug 17, 2026)
publisher: NJ Department of Community Affairs, Division of Codes and Standards
keyFacts: 5:23-1.6 grace period: for 6 months after a subcode revision's operative date, a complete permit application may be reviewed under the prior code (p.29).
5:23-2.7(b)6iii: alteration/replacement/relocation of electrical wiring is NOT ordinary maintenance, except listed items (p.48).

5:23-2.7(c)3 ordinary electrical maintenance (no permit, inspection or notice): like-for-like replacement of receptacles, switches, lighting fixtures (not with emergency battery packs) outside hazardous locations - replacements where GFCI, damp/wet or tamper-resistant required must meet 406.4(D); repairs to installed equipment; Class 3 comms wiring; dishwasher and range-hood replacement; burglar alarm/doorbell in 1-2 family; plug-in irrigation <30 V (pp.52-53).
5:23-2.14(b): ordinary maintenance needs no permit/notice; minor work requires a permit but may begin on notice; emergency work needs a permit application within 72 hours (p.70).

5:23-2.17A minor work (notice before starting, permit application within 5 business days): in 1-2 family dwellings, electrical work incidental to installing A/C, equipment, dryers, ranges/ovens; up to 5 outlets on adequate existing circuits (fishing counts as minor work regardless of number); like-capacity rewiring; also like-for-like device replacement in hazardous locations (pp.132-134).

5:23-2.15: electrical work may only be done by persons licensed under law, except a single-family homeowner on his/her own dwelling; the licensed electrical contractor's seal and signature go on the electrical subcode technical section (pp.86-87).

5:23-2.18(b)1iv(2): required electrical inspections for 1-2 family dwellings are rough wiring, panel and service installation (mid-point), plus final; framing inspection follows rough electrical (pp.140-141).

5:23-2.18(c): request inspections in writing at least 24 hours ahead; performed within 3 business days (or agreed time within 30 days); the request is an attestation that the work is code-compliant (p.142).
5:23-6.1(a)1: other subcodes (incl. the NEC) do not apply to work in existing buildings unless the rehabilitation subcode specifically references them (p.918).
5:23-6.8(d): rehab electrical materials & methods = NEC with exceptions, e.g. 210.11, 210.12 (AFCI), 210.52, 210.63, 210.70 and 110.26 not applied; existing working clearances may remain (p.1006).
5:23-6.9(c): newly installed (not replacement) service equipment/panels must meet 110.26 etc.; newly installed HVAC equipment must meet 210.63(A) and 210.70 (p.1026).
notes: 1622-page consolidated chapter (2.7 MB). Includes rehabilitation subcode (5:23-6), fees (5:23-4) and administrative rules.

title: NJ DCA Construction Code Communicator, Vol. 38 No. 3, Fall 2026
publisher: NJ Department of Community Affairs, Division of Codes and Standards
keyFacts: 2024 I-Codes, 2024 NSPC and 2023 NFPA 70 adopted August 17, 2026; six-month grace period - last day to apply under the previous (2021/2020) codes is February 17, 2027; application should state which code edition was used (p.2).
Electrical technical form F120 revised Dec 2025: fixtures, receptacles and switches combined as 'Devices'; EV chargers and PV systems added (p.4).

Garden State Balcony Solar Act (P.L.2026, c.82, signed Sept 1, 2026): no municipal permit for placing/using plug-in solar devices <=1,200 W (UL 3700); but any receptacle addition/relocation still needs the normal UCC permit (p.5).

DCA guidance: 2023 NEC 210.8(F) Exception No. 2 (listed HVAC equipment) expired Sept 1, 2026; Class A GFCI applies to outdoor outlets for NEWLY installed HVAC, but a like-for-like HVAC replacement in an existing dwelling does not trigger 210.8(F) under the rehab subcode (pp.16-18).
notes: Agency newsletter (guidance, not regulation). Page numbers are PDF pages.

title: P.L.2021, c.479 - Electrical Contractors Licensing Act amendments (Class A journeyman, apprentice, Class B wireman; reciprocity; temporary out-of-state license)
keyFacts: Approved January 18, 2022; effective immediately (p.9).

45:5A-9: no one may work in business as an electrical contractor without a business permit and a licensed electrical contractor (owner/officer/employee) who takes full responsibility; any single act counts as contracting (pp.4-5).
Contractor exam eligibility: 5 years in electrical construction - 1 year as a Class A journeyman plus 4 years in a USDOL-accredited apprenticeship; failed exam retake after 6 months (p.5).
45:5A-11.9: after the 13th month following enactment, no one may perform electrical work unless licensed as an electrical contractor, Class A journeyman, Class A apprentice or Class B wireman (p.9).
Licenses/business permits renew triennially; Class A journeymen and Class B wiremen need a 15-hour course on the most recent NEC each renewal (pp.1, 6).

45:5A-11.7: temporary license without exam for an out-of-state individual as Class A journeyman/apprentice/Class B wireman, max one per triennial period, max 30 days; temporary journeyman works only under a licensed NJ contractor and cannot supervise (p.8).
45:5A-11.8: Board MAY grant licenses without exam to applicants licensed in another state/territory/DC if that jurisdiction gives equal reciprocity to NJ licensees (discretionary) (p.8).

45:5A-18 exemptions from business permit include lamp/fuse replacement, testing/servicing equipment, work under 10 V, and work by a person on a dwelling occupied solely as his/her own residence (pp.6-7).
notes: Official session-law PDF. The Board's implementing rules (N.J.A.C. 13:31; 2024 proposal at 56 N.J.R.) were not retrievable - njconsumeraffairs.gov blocks automated access.

title: Princeton Building Inspections page

keyFacts: Inspection requests must be made at least 48 hours ahead; inspections performed within 3-5 business days (page text) - longer than the state 24-hour/3-business-day rule in 5:23-2.18(c).

Electrical inspection hours Mon-Fri 8 am-2 pm; approved plans must be on site (page text).
